items.title: GTM Rebrands
items.copy:
Clients often plan a global rebrand around a 6-month timeline. Then reality arrives: permit approvals, landlord sign-off, manufacturing lead times, dozens of local systems that don't move on your schedule.
We've seen a single building permit take 15 months because of local hurricane legislation. Combine that with a 12-month IPO deadline and you have a genuine problem.
Bring an execution partner in early. Within a few minutes of reviewing the plans, we can give you a realistic timeline, phased around permitting, landlord cycles and logistics.
Want the full breakdown of the five traps that catch most rebrands out? Read the Execution Gap. Link below.

items.copy:

items.copy: The questions came from months of conversations with procurement leaders across retail, FMCG, financial services and hospitality. items.title: 10 Questions Q2: Risk & resilience
items.copy:
Question two from our ProcureCon 2026 roundtable. The second of the three that ran well ahead of the rest.
Am I managing risk, or just managing the appearance of managing it?
Risk used to mean continuity and cost. Now geopolitics, regulation, cyber and the financial health of suppliers all sit on the same agenda. Most of it moves faster than the quarterly review that’s meant to catch it.
That’s why a tidy dashboard can be the most dangerous thing in the room. No red flags starts to feel like no risk.
The procurement leaders we spoke to weren’t short of reporting. They were short of early warning, especially on single points of failure.
Caught early, risk is value protected. Caught late, it’s a P&L event with your name on it.
Swipe through for what the room said. Comment “review” and we’ll set up a supplier risk review, or read all ten questions at paragonbrandservices.com

items.title: Rebrand killer 2 of 5: The Audit Trap
10 Questions Q3: Cost & value
items.copy:
Question three, and the last of the three that dominated the room at ProcureCon 2026.
When the cuts come, does my value story protect me, or make me the easiest line to delete?
Savings is the most fragile number procurement reports. A headline saving can vanish into rework, rush fees and quality trade-offs that never make the same slide.
And if cost reduction is all finance sees you doing, you’re the first line they cut.
The stronger position talks the business’s language: speed to shelf, fewer write-offs and a brand that looks the same in every store. That means total cost of ownership across print, digital and print-on-demand, not unit price.
It’s how we helped John Lewis cut costs by 66%.
Comment “TCO” to book a total cost of ownership working session, or read all ten questions at paragonbrandservices.com

items.title: 10 Questions Q4: Technology & data
items.copy:
The three dominant questions are done. Question four leads the high-priority tier, and it follows AI everywhere.
Did our technology actually fix the process, or did we just digitise the old one?
Plenty of platforms get bought on the promise of transformation, then automate the same broken process at higher speed. The mess still arrives. It just arrives faster.
Underneath sits a data problem. Most data isn’t ready for the AI layered on top of it: disconnected systems, no shared definitions.
Analytics amplify what they’re given. They don’t repair it.
So fix the process and clean the data first. Then the technology compounds the gains, not the errors. That’s the principle behind RetailOS, now live across 5,000+ retail locations.
Comment “checklist” for our data readiness checklist, or read all ten questions at paragonbrandservices.com

items.title: Rebrand killer 3 of 5: The Making Good Trap
10 Questions Q5: Consolidation & risk
items.copy:
Question five. Every rise in print, paper and logistics costs brings it back.
Should I consolidate, without creating a single point of failure?
The case for consolidation is clear: fewer suppliers, simpler operations, more buying power.
But every supplier you remove is also a fallback you remove. Hand the whole flow to one partner and a single failure can stall everything at once.
So the real question isn’t one partner or many. It’s what sits behind the one. Is it a governed network that spreads the risk, or one place that stacks it?
We run €560m+ of production spend open-book, through a vetted partner network, so you can see where the work goes and what it costs.
